residual.wall: Live hexPapule is odd-r offset plus a Euclidean Gaussian in polar UV. Polar UV is not a hex plane. fu=8 misses odd-row vertices. Fine 18×11 does not tile the 25×40 cage.

question: What hex-lattice algorithms exist, which of them fit a locked 25×40 polar cylinder, and what is the lawful follicle kernel — not a new mesh?
coordinateSpaces: Cage: ring×40+sector, 1000 verts. Polar UV: u=sector/40 wraps, v=ring/24 clamps. Offset odd-r: x=u·fu+(row&1)·½, y=v·fv. Axial (q,r). Cube (q,r,s) with q+r+s=0. Screen is shade-only. Zero field is +0.
physicalLaw: Offset is layout. Axial is storage. Cube is arithmetic (Patel).
A cylinder tiles with hex iff the period divides. A sphere cannot — Euler needs 12 pentagons.
Odd-r sites land on 40-sector vertices iff fu divides 20 (half-step is an integer sector).
P' = P + s n̂ on the same 1000. Topology does not grow.
artisticLaw: Goose is coarse follicles, ~32 rounded mounds on the dermis. Fine is dual-lattice grain, not a second stipple.
Poles stay rest (dermisMask). Remeshing to a geodesic dome is a different body.
Isotropic in the hex metric, then polar-mapped. Do not fake isotropy in offset-UV Euclidean.
